events.title: IBM PC 5150 discontinued
events.summary: IBM discontinued the original Personal Computer 5150 on April 2, 1987 — ending production of the machine that launched the PC-compatible industry.
events.about: The 5150's open architecture spawned thousands of clone makers and made MS-DOS the default PC OS. Its discontinuation marked the handoff to AT-class machines and PS/2 lines, but the ISA expansion bus and BIOS-compatible design outlived the original model by decades. Every x86 laptop and server still carries DNA from this product's form factor.

narrative.whyChosen: The 5150's EOL closed the chapter on IBM's first mass-market personal computer.
narrative.whyImportant: It bookends the platform that defined desktop computing for the next thirty years.
narrative.problemSolved: IBM replaced the aging 5150 with newer models while clones had already commoditized its design.
